content: Please share a complete list of all medications, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John's wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) or SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as an EKG, may be required to monitor your condition. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the time of your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used alone or in combination with other medications to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer treatments (chemotherapy), radiation therapy, or drugs used during surgery. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully when using this medication. To use the oral soluble film, read the patient information leaflet and instructions provided by your pharmacist before starting the medication and each time you get a refill. This film is designed to dissolve on top of your tongue. Do not chew or swallow it whole. With dry hands, open the protective foil pouch just before use, remove one film, and place it on your tongue. Allow it to dissolve completely (usually within 4 to 20 seconds), then swallow it with saliva or liquid. You do not need to take this product with liquid. If your dose requires more than one film, allow each film to dissolve completely before taking the next. To prevent nausea from chemotherapy, take this medication as directed by your doctor, usually 30 minutes before treatment begins. For radiation therapy, take it 1 to 2 hours before the start of treatment. Ondansetron may be taken up to three times a day for 1 to 2 days after each chemotherapy or radiation session. If prescribed on a schedule, take it regularly to maximize its benefits. Dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, dosage may also depend on age and weight. Take this medication exactly as directed. Common side effects include headache, lightheadedness, dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, or constipation. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may increase serotonin levels and cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome or toxicity. The risk is higher if you are taking other drugs that increase serotonin. Inform your doctor or pharmacist of all medications you are taking to avoid interactions. Ondansetron may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can lead to serious complications. The risk is higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if caused by certain medications (e.g., diuretics) or conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Examples of drugs that may interact include MDMA, St. John’s wort, SSRIs, and SNRIs. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
